Forecast Discussion

Thursday’s front is east of the mountains and reaches the coast by evening. Behind it, we have a dry and pleasant Friday with clearing skies.

A second front arrives tonight from the Ohio Valley with much cooler air on a gusty northwest wind. A few sprinkles, maybe a snowflake late at night, are possible along the western escarpment. Saturday is cool, windy, and dry.

High pressure settles over the Tennessee Valley Sunday, and the wind eases. The valleys turn chilly at night under clear skies and dry air. A slow warmup follows Monday and Tuesday as the high moves off the Carolina coast.

A weak front drops in from the north late Tuesday night. It is moisture-starved and only takes a few degrees off Wednesday.

A stronger front crosses the mountains Thursday. It, too, has little moisture to work with, but this one will take a much larger bite out of temperatures by the end of next week. Flurries will be possible on the west side of the Appalachians.
